narrative:
The 2020 Chicago White Sox arrived as one of baseball's most exciting young teams, and a truncated 60-game season gave them the perfect stage to announce themselves. After a rocky July that saw them finish 3-4, the South Siders caught fire in August, posting a scorching 19-9 record that announced them as legitimate contenders in the AL Central. Led by MVP-caliber first baseman José Abreu, electric rookie Luis Robert Jr., and a rotation showing real promise, Chicago played with an energy that hadn't been seen on the South Side in years.

The August surge was the heartbeat of the season. Robert's sharp doubles drove in crucial runs, Eloy Jiménez launched towering home runs, and even Yasmani Grandal delivered in clutch spots. The bullpen occasionally wavered — Alex Colomé's blown save on August 28th was a gut punch — but the lineup's firepower consistently bailed the team out. A 19-9 August run transformed a mediocre start into genuine playoff positioning.

September brought a more complicated story. The White Sox finished 13-12, good enough to clinch a Wild Card berth but marked by some alarming cracks. José Ruiz surrendered a devastating three-run José Ramírez homer on September 22nd that swung nearly a full win in probability. The Cleveland series late in the month exposed vulnerabilities in both the rotation and bullpen, and young pitchers like Dane Dunning and Dylan Cease still had moments where their inexperience showed. Abreu remained a steadying force with a clutch double on September 26th, but the team limped somewhat into October.

The Wild Card round against the Oakland Athletics proved to be the White Sox's undoing. Abreu homered in the opener to give fans hope, but the series quickly unraveled. A costly Nick Madrigal error in Game 2 opened the floodgates, and the bullpen — Evan Marshall and Codi Heuer both surrendering runs — couldn't hold leads. The A's were simply more battle-tested, and Chicago's youth showed at the worst possible time. The loss stung, but it felt less like an ending and more like a prologue to something bigger on the South Side.

chapters.title: Slow Start, High Hopes
chapters.description: Chicago stumbles out of the gate in July before Luis Robert announces his presence with a thunderous August double.

chapters.title: August Dominance
chapters.description: The White Sox catch fire with a 19-9 August, powered by Jiménez home runs and Grandal's clutch blast, despite a bullpen stumble along the way.

chapters.title: Robert Keeps Rolling
chapters.description: Luis Robert's ground-rule double on August 31st caps a statement month and carries momentum into a pivotal September.

chapters.title: September Turbulence
chapters.description: A 13-12 September sees the White Sox clinch a playoff spot but struggle down the stretch against Cleveland, with bullpen meltdowns and young starters getting exposed.

chapters.title: Postseason Heartbreak
chapters.description: The White Sox bow out in the Wild Card round against Oakland, as errors, bullpen woes, and missed opportunities end a promising season short.
